standard_prerequisites.name: Projective bundle formula
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a complex vector bundle E over M of rank k, H^*(P(E)) is the free H^*(M)-algebra on x = c_1(O_{E^*}(1)) subject only to x^k + c_1(E)x^{k-1} + ... + c_k(E) = 0.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the authors' own statement of the convention at source lines 168-169
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the two presentations of H^*(Z_+(M)) in the variables x and x' that the retained computation rewrites and multiplies; no projective-bundle input beyond this is assumed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Poincare dual of the canonical section as a Thom class
standard_prerequisites.statement: For the canonical section s of P(E + C) given pointwise by [0:...:0:1], the Poincare dual of s_*[M] is x^n + c_1x^{n-1} + ... + c_n, the image of the Thom class of the normal bundle.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the article's own Lemma poincaredual, source lines 839-846, delivered here as a context span
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the two twistor sections into explicit degree-six classes in H^*(Z_+(M)); the retained obligation begins after this identification.

standard_prerequisites.name: Spin-c structures as an H^2(M)-torsor
standard_prerequisites.statement: Isomorphism classes of spin-c structures on M form a torsor over H^2(M), and if [s'] = a . [s] then the Hopf bundles of the two projective-bundle models satisfy H' = H (x) L with c_1(L) = a, whence x' = x - a.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the article's own lemma and discussion at source lines 934-940 and 942-972, delivered here as a context span
standard_prerequisites.use: It is exactly what licenses the substitution x' = x + (c_1 - c_1')/2 used in the proof; nothing else about spin-c structures is assumed.

core_obligations: Write the Poincare dual of the section s: M -> Z_+(M) as x^3 + 2c_1x^2 + (c_1^2 + c_2)x + (c_1c_2 - c_3) in the presentation H^*(M)[x]/(x^4 + 2c_1x^3 + (c_1^2+c_2)x^2 + (c_1c_2-c_3)x) of Corollary cohomtwis, and likewise the Poincare dual of s' in the variable x' (source lines 995-999 with context spans 405-419 and 839-846).

Justify the substitution x' = x + (c_1 - c_1')/2 by the torsor relation c_1(a . [s]) = 2a + c_1([s]) and the identity H' = H (x) L of Hopf bundles, so that x' = x - a is a change of generator in one and the same cohomology ring rather than an unrelated notation (context span 942-972 and equation div2 at source lines 974-983).

Rewrite the degree-six class of s'_*[M] in the variable x, multiply it with the degree-six class of s_*[M], and use that x^3 generates H^12(Z_+(M)) over H^6(M) so that the product is x^3 times a class in H^6(M); collect the coefficient (1/8)(c_1^3 + c_1^2c_1' - c_1c_1'^2 - c_1'^3) + (1/2)(c_1c_2' + c_1'c_2') - c_3' (source line 999).

Pair that multiple of x^3 with the fundamental class of Z_+(M) and identify the coefficient with the stated integral, using c_3 = c_3' because both are c_3(TM) (source line 999 and the statement at line 995); the calculation is carried out in rational cohomology so that (1/2)(c_1 - c_1') is unambiguous.
proof_roadmap: Present H^*(Z_+(M)) with respect to J as H^*(M)[x]/(x^4 + 2c_1x^3 + (c_1^2+c_2)x^2 + (c_1c_2-c_3)x), and with respect to J' in the variable x' by the same formula in c_i'.
Use Lemma poincaredual for the canonical section of P(C + Lambda^2_C TM) = Z_+(M) to write both Poincare duals as degree-six classes.
Recall x' = x + (c_1 - c_1')/2 from equation div2, whose proof is the spin-c comparison lemma, and substitute it into the class of s'_*[M].
Multiply the two classes; degree bookkeeping in the projective-bundle presentation leaves x^3 times a class in H^6(M); read off the coefficient and pair with [Z_+(M)].
difficulty_reason: The statement fixes two orthogonal almost complex structures J and J' inducing the same orientation on a closed Riemannian six-manifold and asks for the homological intersection number of the two induced sections of the positive twistor space, a pairing that exists only because two six-dimensional fibres meet in a twelve-dimensional total space. The proof must first write each section as an explicit degree-six class in the projective-bundle presentation H^*(M)[x]/(x^4 + 2c_1x^3 + (c_1^2+c_2)x^2 + (c_1c_2-c_3)x) of Corollary cohomtwis, then replace x' by x + (c_1-c_1')/2 (equation div2, whose proof is the spin-c comparison lemma at source lines 942-972) and multiply the two classes. The part that cannot be done routinely is that x' is not a free second variable: it is tied to x by the H^2(M)-torsor of spin-c structures, the substitution is unambiguous only in rational cohomology, and the collapse of the product to x^3 times a class in H^6(M) has to be read off from the ring relation rather than assumed (source lines 998-999).
